In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the value of active therapy for persons with mild hypertension remains uncertain.
drug treatment should be considered for patients with mild hypertension if they are at high risk of cardiovascular complications and if the risk of drug treatment is low, as it is for most patients.

the treatment of mild hypertension in most patients is not yet proved to be of benefit, but that it is reasonable to treat such patients with drug therapy, especially when the risks of disease outweigh the risks of therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the "push to treat," although not yet proven to be correct, is based on the best evidence that is available at present.
the "push to treat mild hypertension" has been too strong.
the risk of cardiovascular disease in patients with mild hypertension should be assessed, and the decision to treat should be based on the risk-benefit ratio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lot of variation in the way that doctors manage hypertension.
the risk of disease is not the same as the risk of treatment.
we need to do more to understand how the environment and lifestyle factors influence our health, especially for people with hypertension.
